short: A Mongol flanking column destroyed the chivalry of Poland and Silesia in a single morning.
full:
The force that entered Poland in 1241 was a screen, perhaps two tumens under Baidar and Kadan, sent to keep the northern powers from reinforcing Hungary. It burned Kraków, found it abandoned, and moved west into Silesia. Duke Henry II the Pious gathered Polish levies, Silesian miners, and small contingents of Templars and other military orders, and gave battle at Legnica on 9 April without waiting for King Wenceslaus of Bohemia, who was two days' march away.

The pattern was the one used everywhere that spring. Mongol light horse skirmished, withdrew, and drew the knights forward into arrow fire and smoke; the Polish cavalry, once separated from the infantry, was enveloped and ridden down. Henry was killed trying to escape and his head was paraded on a lance before Legnica's walls. The Mongols did not occupy Poland — they turned south to rejoin Batu, having achieved exactly what they were sent to do, two days before the main army broke Hungary at Mohi.
